segments.text: Marsh Board spillway annual record. This packet contains field notes, proposed releases, signed closures and an index of the records transferred to the river control desk. The field procedures describe collection of evidence and can precede a final authorization by several shifts. Each team logs its work under the numbered place in the appendix. When a local note conflicts with a signed decision, apply the decision for the site and record in question. Duplicate counts in handwritten tables are retained as audit evidence. The final decisions distinguish the upper floodgates and the lower access roads.

Appendix entry 01 for Upper Fork. The lead marked 11 level marks in the handoff ledger and sent a copy to the river control desk. The morning crew performed a paired staff-gauge reading and left the local barrier in place. A second observer compared the identifying marks with the original register. The storage label indicated where a duplicate packet could be found, rather than when a particular restriction ended. A canceled entry mentioned a 15-minute closure. It was kept in the file to document the sequence of earlier decisions. The receiving crew added arrival and departure readings under separate date lines so neither number overwrote a signed record.
During review of Upper Fork, the team noted differences between the location diagram and the supplied marker list. The diagram was reissued to show which side of the access boundary could be used by the maintenance crew. The supervisor did not approve unscheduled changes based on the diagram alone. The packet lists the original contact at the start and the person who accepted the record at the end. General advice for nearby locations has been retained for planning, while final instructions only apply to the named location. The archive treats the countersignature and specific condition as part of each final decision.

What readings and interval must river control countersign before reopening the Canal East service road under CE-71?

expected_answers: Two upstream readings below 1.20 m, 45 minutes apart, both countersigned by river control.
